paragraph: Hackensack runs four tiers, and the volume sits in condos. Single-family closed 36 sales over six months at a median of $650,000, with a sale-to-list ratio of 1.003 and a median 21 days on market. About 58 percent went above asking, so this is competitive but not frenzied. Priced homes are moving, and the spread from $380,000 to $1,190,000 is wide enough that the median is the number to trust. Multi-family is the smaller, higher-priced tier at 12 sales and a median of $785,000, moving in roughly 19 days at essentially full list. Condos and townhouses carry the market with 82 sales at a median of $320,000, a ratio of exactly 1.00, and 29 days on market, with about a third selling above ask. Co-ops are thin at 8 sales and a median of $201,000, closing slightly under list after 43 days, and they come with board approval, financing restrictions, and resale friction that not every buyer is aware of going in. On the monthly numbers, single-family has held flat to slightly firmer through July while condo medians have drifted down on steady volume, which reads as mix shifting toward smaller units rather than values dropping. If you're comparing tiers, the deciding factor isn't market heat. It's whether you want the space and grounds of a single-family, the rental income of a multi-family, the low-maintenance lifestyle of a condo, or the lower price point of a co-op.
